newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl calls on Germans to abandon "macho" thinking.
newsitem.headline: Kohl calls on Germans to abandon "macho" thinking.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl said in an interview published on Saturday there was still too much "macho thinking" in Germany and urged his Christian Democratic Union (CDU) party to adopt quotas for women at its annual conference.

Kohl said continued male dominance of the upper echelons of German society showed reform was needed and his party could play its part by adopting quotas at this year's conference, due to begin in Hanover on Sunday.

"There's still a considerable amount of macho thinking. If you look at the top ranks of German industry for example, you don't see many women there," Kohl told the Hannoversche Allgemeine Zeitung daily.
"We must push forward a learning process which is only progressing very slowly, not just in the party but everywhere in society," the veteran chancellor said.
Ar last year's conference the CDU narrowly rejected a resolution to adopt women's quotas despite support from Kohl.
